hydrograph.title: Storm Hydrograph
hydrograph.description: Illustrative catchment response. Sliders are relative scenario settings, not measured percentages or a calibrated flood forecast. Compare the rainfall peak with the discharge peak to read lag time.
hydrograph.subduedNote: In this scenario the response is broader and the peak later. Actual shape also depends on basin size, slope, soils and storm duration.
hydrograph.flashyNote: In this scenario the response is faster with a higher peak. This illustrates a tendency, not a prediction for a real catchment.

circulation.title: Atmospheric Circulation
circulation.description: Explore a schematic long-term, zonally averaged circulation model. Pressure belts and boundaries migrate; continents, oceans and seasons create regional differences.
circulation.hoverHint: Hover a cell to see its description.
circulation.legendLow: L = relatively low pressure; ascent often supports clouds and rain
circulation.legendHigh: H = relatively high pressure; descent often suppresses cloud
circulation.summary: Approximate pattern: tropical ascent, subtropical descent, subpolar ascent and polar descent. This helps explain climate belts but is not a weather forecast.

hadleyN.name: Hadley (N)
hadleyN.desc: A tropical overturning circulation: air rises near the shifting tropical rain belt, moves poleward aloft and generally sinks in the subtropics. Surface trade winds return air toward the convergence zone.

ferrelN.name: Ferrel (N)
ferrelN.desc: The idealised mid-latitude mean circulation, with surface air generally moving poleward and an equatorward return aloft. It is thermally indirect and maintained largely through mid-latitude weather systems and their heat and momentum transfers.

polarN.name: Polar (N)
polarN.desc: In the idealised circulation model, cold air sinks at high latitudes and flows equatorward near the surface, with ascent toward subpolar latitudes and return flow aloft.

polarS.name: Polar (S)
polarS.desc: In the idealised circulation model, cold air sinks at high latitudes and flows equatorward near the surface, with ascent toward subpolar latitudes and return flow aloft.

ferrelS.name: Ferrel (S)
ferrelS.desc: The idealised mid-latitude mean circulation, with surface air generally moving poleward and an equatorward return aloft. It is thermally indirect and maintained largely through mid-latitude weather systems and their heat and momentum transfers.

hadleyS.name: Hadley (S)
hadleyS.desc: A tropical overturning circulation: air rises near the shifting tropical rain belt, moves poleward aloft and generally sinks in the subtropics. Surface trade winds return air toward the convergence zone.

fieldwork.title: Fieldwork & Research
fieldwork.intro: How geographers gather and interpret data — explicitly on the teacher's revision checklist. Knowing this vocabulary unlocks the long-answer Criterion B questions on the exam.

aim.name: Aim
aim.rule: The question or purpose that the investigation is designed to address. It specifies what will be studied and where.
examples: Aim: investigate how channel width changes along a selected river reach.

contrast.en: An aim asks what to investigate; a hypothesis proposes a testable answer.
contrast.ru: Цель задаёт направление исследования; гипотеза предлагает проверяемый ответ.

sources.title: Royal Geographical Society — Rural investigations

hypothesis.name: Hypothesis
hypothesis.rule: A testable statement about an expected relationship or difference. Identify measurable variables and collect evidence that could support or challenge it.
examples: Hypothesis: mean channel width increases with distance downstream in this reach.

contrast.en: Evidence may support a hypothesis within the sample; it does not prove a universal rule.
contrast.ru: Данные могут поддержать гипотезу для выборки, но не доказывают универсальное правило.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introduction to Sociology 3e
sources.section: 2.1 Scientific method: Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5; reliability and validity

nullHypothesis.name: Null hypothesis (H₀)
nullHypothesis.rule: The statistical baseline tested against an alternative; in a simple fieldwork test it usually states no population difference or association between the specified variables.
examples: H₀: there is no association between distance downstream and channel width in the population being studied.

contrast.en: Failing to reject H₀ is not proof that no relationship exists: the sample may be too small or noisy.
contrast.ru: Если H₀ не отвергнута, это ещё не доказательство отсутствия связи: выборка может быть слишком мала или неточна.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 9.1 Null and alternative hypotheses

primary.name: Primary data
primary.rule: Evidence collected first-hand for the present investigation, using an explicit method such as measurement, observation or an interview.
examples: Your river-depth measurements and your recorded interview responses are both primary data.

contrast.en: Primary/secondary describes origin; quantitative/qualitative describes the kind of information.
contrast.ru: Первичные/вторичные — происхождение; количественные/качественные — характер информации.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introduction to Sociology 3e
sources.section: 2.2 Research methods: research design; Field Research; Secondary Data Analysis

secondary.name: Secondary data
secondary.rule: Existing evidence reused for an investigation, originally collected by someone else or for another purpose. Check its date, scale, definitions and collection method.
examples: A published rainfall series used to interpret your river measurements is secondary data.

contrast.en: Secondary does not mean unreliable; official records may cover more places and years than a class survey.
contrast.ru: Вторичные не означает ненадёжные: официальные ряды могут охватывать больше мест и лет, чем школьное обследование.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introduction to Sociology 3e
sources.section: 2.2 Research methods: research design; Field Research; Secondary Data Analysis

quantitative.name: Quantitative data
quantitative.rule: Numerical counts or measurements of a quantity. Counts are usually discrete; measurements such as depth are continuous, although recorded to finite precision.
examples: 12 pedestrians in five minutes is a count; 0.42 m water depth is a measurement.

contrast.en: A numerical category code is not automatically a measured quantity.
contrast.ru: Числовой код категории не становится от этого измеренной величиной.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

qualitative.name: Qualitative data
qualitative.rule: Descriptions or categories expressing characteristics, meanings or experiences, such as land-use type or interview accounts. They can be coded and compared systematically.
examples: Residential, retail and park are land-use categories; interview comments add explanations.

contrast.en: Qualitative is not a synonym for opinion or poor quality; a land-use category can be directly observed.
contrast.ru: Качественные — не синоним субъективных или плохих данных: категорию землепользования можно наблюдать непосредственно.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

sampleSize.name: Sample size
sampleSize.rule: The number of observational units included in a sample, written n. State whether a unit is a person, site, pebble or independent measurement.
examples: Thirty pebbles at one site describe that site, not thirty independent river sites.

contrast.en: A larger sample can reduce random sampling error; it cannot automatically remove selection bias.
contrast.ru: Большая выборка может уменьшить случайную ошибку, но сама по себе не устраняет систематический перекос отбора.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

systematic.name: Systematic sampling
systematic.rule: Select observations at a fixed interval from an ordered population or along space/time, ideally after a randomly chosen starting point.
examples: From a random starting point, record land use every 50 m along the route.

contrast.en: Regular spacing is efficient, but can coincide with a repeating pattern and bias the sample.
contrast.ru: Равные интервалы удобны, но могут совпасть с повторяющейся структурой и исказить выборку.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

stratified.name: Stratified sampling
stratified.rule: Divide the population into relevant non-overlapping groups, then sample within every group. In proportional stratified sampling, each group supplies its share of the sample.
examples: If 40% of residents are in one age group, a proportional sample of 50 includes 20 from that group.

contrast.en: Stratified sampling includes each stratum; cluster sampling selects only some whole groups.
contrast.ru: Стратификация охватывает каждую группу; кластерный отбор выбирает лишь часть целых групп.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

random.name: Simple random sampling
random.rule: Use a random procedure so every possible sample of a given size has an equal chance of selection from the defined population.
examples: Number all eligible sites and use a random-number generator to select them.

contrast.en: Choosing whoever is easiest to reach is convenience sampling, even if it feels unplanned.
contrast.ru: Выбор тех, к кому проще подойти, — удобная выборка, даже если он кажется бессистемным.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.body: A methodology explains and justifies how the investigation is conducted: sites, sampling, timing, equipment, measurement procedure, data handling and practical constraints. Give enough detail for repetition and explain how choices affect the question being answered.

bar.name: Bar chart
bar.rule: Separate bars compare counts or values for categories. Label the categories, quantity and units; normally start the value axis at zero so bar lengths remain comparable.
examples: Compare pedestrian counts at three named sites during equal five-minute intervals.

contrast.en: A histogram groups numerical data into intervals; its bars have a different meaning from category bars.
contrast.ru: Гистограмма группирует числовые данные по интервалам; её столбцы означают не то же, что столбцы категорий.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 2.1 Line graphs and bar graphs

line.name: Line graph
line.rule: Plot values in a meaningful sequence, usually against time or distance, and join adjacent observations to show change.
examples: Plot river discharge in m³/s against time in hours.

contrast.en: A connecting line implies an ordered continuum; it does not establish values between measurements as observed facts.
contrast.ru: Соединение точек предполагает упорядоченную непрерывную шкалу; промежуточные значения от этого не становятся измеренными.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 2.1 Line graphs and bar graphs

scatter.name: Scatter graph
scatter.rule: Each point shows a paired observation of two quantitative variables. The pattern helps identify direction, strength, outliers and possible non-linear relationships.
examples: Plot each site's distance downstream against its measured channel width.

contrast.en: Correlation does not establish causation; another variable or sampling pattern may explain the association.
contrast.ru: Корреляция не доказывает причинность: связь может объясняться третьей переменной или особенностями отбора.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 12.3 Scatter plots, regression and cautions about interpretation

pie.name: Pie chart
pie.rule: Sectors represent mutually exclusive parts of one complete total. Sector angle = category value ÷ total × 360°.
examples: A category containing 25% of the total occupies 90°.

contrast.en: Use a bar chart if respondents can choose multiple overlapping categories; those shares need not sum to 100%.
contrast.ru: Если можно выбрать несколько пересекающихся категорий, используй столбчатую диаграмму: такие доли не обязаны давать 100%.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introductory Statistics 2e
sources.section: 1.2 Data, sampling, graphs and sampling bias

gis.name: Geographic information system (GIS)
gis.rule: A computer-based system for storing, linking, analysing and displaying data referenced to geographic locations, often as map layers.
examples: Overlay buildings, elevation and a flood-extent layer to identify exposed properties.

contrast.en: A GIS is an analysis system; a GPS/GNSS receiver estimates a position that can supply data to it.
contrast.ru: ГИС — система анализа; приёмник GPS/ГНСС определяет координаты, которые могут стать её исходными данными.

sources.title: USGS — What is a geographic information system?

analysis.title: Data analysis
analysis.body: Spearman’s rank correlation measures the direction and strength of a monotonic association using ranks, from −1 to +1. Zero means no ranked monotonic association, not necessarily no relationship. Statistical significance requires a suitable method accounting for sample size, ties and test direction; association does not prove causation.

contrast.en: The coefficient measures monotonic association, not causation; statistical significance is a separate question. A constant variable has no defined rank correlation.
contrast.ru: Коэффициент измеряет монотонную связь, а не причинность; статистическая значимость — отдельный вопрос. Для постоянной переменной ранговая корреляция не определена.

sources.title: SciPy scientific documentation — Spearman rank correlation

conclusion.name: Conclusion
conclusion.rule: An evidence-based answer to the investigation aim. Refer to measured patterns, relevant values and exceptions, and state how far the hypothesis is supported.
examples: Width rose at four of five sites; the bridge site differed, so support is qualified.

contrast.en: A conclusion answers the question; an evaluation assesses the evidence and method behind that answer.
contrast.ru: Вывод отвечает на вопрос; оценка исследования рассматривает данные и методы, на которых он основан.

sources.title: OpenStax — Introduction to Sociology 3e
sources.section: 2.1 Scientific method: Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5; reliability and validity

evaluation.name: Evaluation
evaluation.rule: Judge how sampling, measurement, timing and analysis affect the trustworthiness and scope of the conclusion. Link each limitation to a feasible improvement.
examples: Repeat counts at different times to test whether one lunchtime represented the day.

contrast.en: Reliability concerns consistency; validity concerns whether the method answers the intended question. Repetition alone cannot fix a biased method.
contrast.ru: Надёжность касается воспроизводимости; валидность — соответствия метода исследовательскому вопросу. Повторение само по себе не исправляет смещённый метод.

tectonics.title: Plate tectonics
tectonics.body: Tectonic plates are pieces of lithosphere: crust plus rigid uppermost mantle. They move over weaker, mostly solid upper mantle. Gravity acting on subducting slabs and elevated ridges, together with mantle flow, contributes to motion. Divergent, convergent and transform boundaries describe relative plate movement; continental collision is one convergent setting.

contrast.en: Plates contain crust and uppermost mantle; crust alone is not a plate.
contrast.ru: Плита включает кору и верхнюю мантию; одна кора не образует плиту.

urbanisation.title: Urbanisation
urbanisation.body: Urbanisation is an increase in the share of a population living in urban settlements, alongside wider changes associated with urban life. Rural-to-urban migration is one contributor; natural increase and settlement reclassification also matter. Urban population growth means rising numbers and can occur without a rising urban share.

contrast.en: An increasing urban population is not necessarily an increasing urban share.
contrast.ru: Рост числа горожан не обязательно означает рост их доли.

globalisation.title: Globalisation
items: Globalisation is the development of connections and interdependence across national borders through trade, investment, migration, information and culture.
It differs from development: stronger connections do not guarantee better health, education or living standards for everyone.
Benefits and costs differ within countries and between groups; avoid assuming all firms or all workers win or lose.

contrast.en: Cross-border connections and human development are different ideas.
contrast.ru: Трансграничные связи и человеческое развитие — разные понятия.

sustainable.title: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
sustainable.body: Seventeen linked global goals adopted in 2015 as part of the UN 2030 Agenda. They set objectives supported by targets and indicators for countries at all income levels.

contrast.en: Goals, measurable targets and indicators have distinct roles.
contrast.ru: Цели, конкретные задачи и показатели выполняют разные роли.

biomes.title: World biomes
items: A biome is a large ecological grouping characterised by climate, vegetation and associated organisms; its boundaries are gradual and classifications differ.
Tropical rainforest: warm, wet conditions favour dense forest. Savanna: seasonal water availability supports grasses with scattered trees.
Deserts: limited available moisture; they can be hot or cold. Temperate forests include different seasonal and rainfall regimes.
Boreal forest (taiga): long cold winters, mostly coniferous trees. Tundra: low-growing vegetation and a short growing season; permafrost is widespread in Arctic tundra.

contrast.en: A biome groups ecological communities over large areas; an ecosystem describes organisms and their physical environment interacting at a chosen scale.
contrast.ru: Биом объединяет экологические сообщества обширных территорий; экосистема описывает взаимодействие организмов и среды в выбранном масштабе.

sources.title: OpenStax — Biology 2e

development.title: Human development
development.body: Human development means expanding people’s capabilities, opportunities and choices to live lives they value. Health, education and access to resources matter alongside participation and freedom. Economic growth can support development but its benefits may be distributed unequally.

contrast.en: Income is one means of improving life; GDP alone does not measure health, learning, choices or inequality.
contrast.ru: Доход — одно из средств улучшения жизни; ВВП сам по себе не измеряет здоровье, образование, свободу выбора и неравенство.

rivers.title: Distinctive Landscapes — Rivers
rivers.intro: How rivers shape the land: from source to mouth, processes of erosion and transportation, landform formation, flooding and management.

bradshaw.title: Bradshaw Model
bradshaw.description: The Bradshaw model summarises common downstream trends: discharge, width, depth and mean velocity tend to increase, while gradient and typical sediment size tend to decrease. These are tendencies, not laws; geology, tributaries, dams and water abstraction can interrupt them. Slider values are illustrative, not measurements or predictions.

course.title: River Course
course.description: Upper, middle and lower course describe relative position along a river. Erosion, transport and deposition can all occur within each; their balance varies with local conditions.

abrasion.name: Abrasion (corrasion)
abrasion.rule: Sediment carried by a river scrapes, grinds or strikes the bed and banks, wearing them away. The load acts as an abrasive tool.
examples: Gravel swirled in a bedrock hollow can grind a pothole.

contrast.en: Abrasion wears the channel; attrition wears the transported fragments. Russian «абразия» most often refers to coastal wave erosion, so the process is spelled out here.
contrast.ru: Abrasion разрушает русло; attrition истирает сами переносимые обломки. Русское «абразия» чаще относится к разрушению берегов волнами, поэтому здесь дано описание процесса.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

attrition.name: Attrition
attrition.rule: Transported rock fragments collide with one another and the channel, chipping off edges and becoming smaller and usually rounder.
examples: A newly broken angular pebble becomes smoother during repeated transport; rock hardness also matters.

contrast.en: Attrition changes the load. Abrasion is the associated wearing of the bed or banks; both can occur in one collision.
contrast.ru: Attrition изменяет сами наносы. Abrasion — сопутствующее разрушение дна или берегов; один удар может участвовать в обоих процессах.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

sources.title: Litwin Miller & Jerolmack — Controls on the rates and products of particle attrition by bed-load collisions
sources.section: Abstract and 1 Introduction: impact attrition; terminology varies across disciplines

model.en: School geography often reserves abrasion for wear of the bed/banks and attrition for wear of the load. Research literature sometimes uses abrasion more broadly; identify the material being worn.
model.ru: В школьной географии abrasion обычно обозначает истирание дна/берегов, а attrition — самих наносов. В научной литературе abrasion иногда употребляют шире; уточняй, какой материал разрушается.

hydraulicAction.name: Hydraulic action
hydraulicAction.rule: The force and pressure fluctuations of moving water loosen and remove material from the bed or banks. Water entering cracks can help detach jointed rock.
examples: Fast turbulent water can remove loose bank material even without gravel grinding it.

contrast.en: Hydraulic action needs the water's force; abrasion needs sediment striking or scraping the channel. Trapped-air pressure is one mechanism, not the whole definition.
contrast.ru: При hydraulic action действует сила воды; при abrasion — удары и трение наносов о русло. Давление запертого воздуха — лишь один механизм, а не полное определение.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

solution.name: Solution (corrosion)
solution.rule: Soluble minerals dissolve through chemical interaction with river water and are removed in solution. Slightly acidic water can dissolve carbonate minerals in limestone.
examples: Calcium and bicarbonate ions can leave a limestone reach in clear water.

contrast.en: Dissolving the bed is a chemical erosion/weathering process; carrying the resulting ions is transport in solution.
contrast.ru: Растворение дна — химическое разрушение; перенос образовавшихся ионов — транспорт в растворе.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

traction.name: Traction
traction.rule: Sediment moves along the bed by rolling or sliding under the force of the flow. It is one form of bed-load transport.
examples: A gravel clast rolls along the bed during high flow.

contrast.en: There is no universal pebble-size boundary: movement depends on flow, grain size, shape and density.
contrast.ru: Универсальной границы размера нет: движение зависит от потока, размера, формы и плотности частиц.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

saltation.name: Saltation
saltation.rule: Particles move in short hops, repeatedly lifted from the bed and returned to it. Saltation connects rolling bed load with suspended transport.
examples: Sand grains bounce downstream close to the bed.

contrast.en: Saltation means repeated bed contact; suspension keeps particles within the flow for longer.
contrast.ru: При сальтации частица снова касается дна; во взвеси она дольше остаётся внутри потока.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

suspension.name: Suspension
suspension.rule: Solid particles are carried within the water column, supported by turbulent motion against settling. Fine silt and clay commonly travel this way.
examples: Cloudy river water can contain fine suspended sediment.

contrast.en: Suspended material remains solid; dissolved material exists as dissolved ions or molecules.
contrast.ru: Взвешенный материал остаётся твёрдым; растворённое вещество находится в виде ионов или молекул.

sources.title: Steven Earle — Physical Geology, 2nd edition (BCcampus)
sources.section: 13.3 Stream erosion and deposition; Figures 13.3.1–13.3.3

solution.name: Dissolved load (transport in solution)
solution.rule: Dissolved substances travel with the river water as ions or molecules. Their transport does not require the water to support solid grains against gravity.
examples: Dissolved salts travel even in water with little visible sediment.

contrast.en: Clear water can carry a substantial dissolved load. Deposition by settling applies to particles, not directly to dissolved ions.
contrast.ru: Прозрачная вода может нести много растворённых веществ. Оседание относится к частицам, а не непосредственно к растворённым ионам.

stages.1: Hard rock overlies soft rock; soft rock is eroded faster
stages.2: A plunge pool forms at the base of the drop
stages.3: An overhang develops as soft rock is eroded back
stages.4: Overhang collapses; waterfall retreats upstream, leaving a gorge

meander.title: Meander & oxbow lake
meander.description: A meander is a river bend. In a typical bend, faster flow and erosion near the outer bank accompany deposition on the inner point bar. Migration may narrow the neck until a cutoff leaves an oxbow lake; not every bend follows this sequence.

drainageBasin.title: Drainage basin
drainageBasin.description: A drainage basin (catchment) is the area supplying water to a river system through a common outlet. A drainage divide separates neighbouring basins. Inputs such as precipitation move through stores and pathways: interception, infiltration into soil, throughflow, groundwater flow and surface runoff; evaporation and transpiration return water to the atmosphere.

hydrograph.title: Storm hydrograph
hydrograph.description: A hydrograph plots river discharge against time. A storm hydrograph shows the response to rainfall: rising limb, peak discharge and falling limb. Here lag time is measured from peak rainfall intensity to peak discharge; other conventions must be stated explicitly.

flooding.title: Causes of flooding
flooding.physical: Physical: prolonged rainfall, saturated ground, snowmelt, steep relief, impermeable rock
flooding.human: Human: deforestation, urbanisation, poor drainage, climate change

prolongedRain.name: Prolonged or intense rainfall
prolongedRain.rule: Intense rainfall can exceed infiltration capacity; prolonged rainfall can fill soil and catchment stores. Both can increase runoff and river discharge.
examples: A short intense storm and a long wet spell may cause flooding by different pathways.

contrast.en: Intensity is rainfall per unit time; total rainfall also depends on duration and spatial coverage.
contrast.ru: Интенсивность — количество осадков за единицу времени; сумма зависит также от длительности и площади дождя.

saturatedGround.name: Antecedent conditions and saturation
saturatedGround.rule: Antecedent conditions describe the catchment before the storm. Where soil pores are already filled with water, there is little remaining storage and additional rain can become rapid runoff.
examples: Two equal storms can produce different peaks after a dry week and after a wet week.

contrast.en: Saturation is water-filled pore space; impermeability concerns the difficulty of water moving through material.
contrast.ru: Насыщение — заполнение пор водой; водонепроницаемость — затруднённое движение воды через материал.

snowmelt.name: Snowmelt
snowmelt.rule: Melting releases water previously stored as snow. Rapid warming or rain on snow can deliver much meltwater to channels over a short period.
examples: Spring snowmelt can raise discharge even without heavy rain at the gauging station.

contrast.en: Snowfall stores water; the runoff response depends on when it melts and whether the ground can absorb it.
contrast.ru: Снегопад запасает воду; сток зависит от времени таяния и способности грунта впитывать воду.

reliefRock.name: Relief and permeability
reliefRock.rule: Steep slopes can speed surface runoff. Low-permeability soil or rock restricts infiltration and subsurface flow, favouring rapid delivery to channels.
examples: A steep, wet catchment with compacted soils may respond rapidly to intense rainfall.

contrast.en: Relief alone does not determine flooding: vegetation, soils, drainage and storm position also matter.
contrast.ru: Рельеф не определяет паводок в одиночку: важны растительность, почвы, дренаж и положение ливня.

deforestation.name: Deforestation and runoff
deforestation.rule: Removing trees can reduce rainfall interception and evapotranspiration. Soil disturbance or compaction may also reduce infiltration and increase rapid runoff.
examples: Logging tracks can channel water quickly toward streams.

contrast.en: The effect varies with catchment scale, soils and storm size; trees cannot prevent every flood.
contrast.ru: Эффект зависит от масштаба бассейна, почв и силы дождя; лес не предотвращает любое наводнение.

urbanisation.name: Urban surfaces and drainage
urbanisation.rule: Roofs, roads and connected drains can reduce infiltration and route rainwater rapidly to rivers, shortening response time and increasing the peak after a storm.
examples: Rain gardens and permeable surfaces can reduce rapid runoff where local conditions allow.

contrast.en: Urbanisation means a growing urban share of population; sealing land and drainage connections explain the hydrological effect.
contrast.ru: Урбанизация — рост доли городского населения; гидрологический эффект объясняют покрытие земли и устройство водоотвода.

climate.name: Climate change and flood risk
climate.rule: Climate change can alter heavy rainfall, snowmelt and sea level, changing flood hazard. Exposure and vulnerability determine how those changes translate into losses.
examples: More intense rainfall can increase runoff, but local flood trends also depend on land use and management.

contrast.en: A global tendency does not mean every river floods more often; regional circulation and catchment changes matter.
contrast.ru: Глобальная тенденция не означает учащения паводков на каждой реке: важны региональная циркуляция и изменения бассейна.

management.hard: Hard engineering: dams, embankments, channel straightening, flood walls
management.soft: Soft engineering: floodplain zoning, afforestation, river restoration, warnings

dams.name: Dams and reservoirs
dams.rule: A dam impounds water; a reservoir used for flood control stores part of an incoming flood and releases it more slowly when safe downstream capacity is available.
examples: Benefit: reduce a flood peak. Trade-off: inundated land, sediment trapping and altered downstream flows.

contrast.en: A reservoir needs spare storage and suitable operation; a full reservoir cannot absorb unlimited floodwater.
contrast.ru: Нужны свободный объём и подходящий режим управления; заполненное водохранилище не может принять неограниченный паводок.

embankments.name: Flood embankments (artificial levees)
embankments.rule: Raised earth barriers along a river restrict floodwater from spreading onto protected land, up to their design and maintenance limits.
examples: Overtopping or breach can flood land behind a barrier; residual risk remains.

contrast.en: Artificial flood defences differ from natural levees built by river sediment deposition.
contrast.ru: Искусственные защитные дамбы отличаются от естественных прирусловых валов, созданных отложением наносов.

channelStraightening.name: Channel straightening
channelStraightening.rule: Removing bends shortens a channel reach and can increase its slope and flow conveyance, moving water more quickly through the modified reach.
examples: Assess the whole catchment before claiming that a faster channel reduces overall flood risk.

contrast.en: Faster passage at one location can transfer a flood problem downstream and damage river habitats.
contrast.ru: Ускорение воды в одном месте может переносить проблему вниз по течению и нарушать речные местообитания.

floodWalls.name: Flood walls
floodWalls.rule: Engineered walls keep floodwater away from particular buildings or urban areas up to a specified protection level.
examples: A wall saves space compared with a broad earth embankment but needs inspection and maintenance.

contrast.en: Protection reduces risk but cannot guarantee safety for every event; drainage behind the wall also matters.
contrast.ru: Защита снижает риск, но не гарантирует безопасность при любом событии; важен и водоотвод за стеной.

floodplainZoning.name: Floodplain zoning
floodplainZoning.rule: Land-use planning limits vulnerable development in areas expected to flood and can reserve space for water storage or low-damage uses.
examples: A riverside park may tolerate temporary inundation better than a hospital on the same site.

contrast.en: Zoning mainly reduces exposure; it does not stop the river rising.
contrast.ru: Зонирование прежде всего уменьшает подверженность; уровень реки при этом всё равно может расти.

afforestation.name: Afforestation and catchment woodland
afforestation.rule: Establishing woodland can increase interception and soil infiltration and slow some runoff pathways, depending on site and management.
examples: Target woodland where it can interrupt rapid runoff; allow time for soils and vegetation to develop.

contrast.en: Afforestation is establishing forest on land not recently forested; it is not an immediate guarantee against extreme floods.
contrast.ru: Лесоразведение — создание леса на земле без недавнего лесного покрова; это не немедленная гарантия от экстремальных паводков.

restoration.name: River restoration
restoration.rule: Restoring channel and floodplain processes can reconnect storage areas, recreate bends or wetlands, and improve habitat while managing flood flows.
examples: Reconnect a suitable floodplain so part of a flood spreads and is stored away from vulnerable buildings.

contrast.en: Restoration does not mean flooding is eliminated; some land is deliberately allowed to flood to reduce damage elsewhere.
contrast.ru: Восстановление не устраняет затопление: часть земли намеренно оставляют для разлива, снижая ущерб в других местах.

warnings.name: Flood forecasts and warnings
warnings.rule: Forecasts estimate possible river levels or flooding from observations and models. Warnings communicate danger and actions so people can prepare and respond.
examples: Move possessions and use an agreed evacuation plan before routes become flooded.

contrast.en: A warning reduces consequences only if it reaches people in time and they can act; it does not reduce the rainfall itself.
contrast.ru: Предупреждение уменьшает последствия, если приходит вовремя и люди могут действовать; сам дождь оно не ослабляет.

boscastle.title: Case study — Boscastle floods 2004
boscastle.summary: On 16 August 2004, intense rainfall caused a flash flood through Boscastle, Cornwall. Rivers overtopped, buildings were damaged and vehicles were swept away. The Met Office records no deaths and a major helicopter rescue operation.

seep.social: Social: people required urgent rescue and temporary shelter.
seep.economic: Economic: homes, businesses, roads and bridges were damaged; the Environment Agency reports about 115 vehicles swept away.
seep.environmental: Environmental: floodwater moved large amounts of sediment and debris; sewers were damaged.
seep.political: Governance: the Environment Agency and local partners coordinated flood defences and community flood planning.

responses.government: Government and partners: new river and rainfall monitoring supported a tailored warning service.
responses.shortTerm: Short term: around 4,000 tonnes of debris were removed, according to the Environment Agency’s 2014 retrospective.
responses.longTerm: Long term: channel and bridge changes, culverts and community planning; the 2014 retrospective reports over £10 million in improvements, a different measure from total flood damage.

mass.name: Mass tourism
mass.rule: Tourism involving large visitor flows and services organised on a large scale, often concentrated in popular resorts and supported by standardised transport and accommodation.
examples: A coastal resort with large hotels and package holidays illustrates the pattern; visitor volume alone does not measure local benefit.

contrast.en: Mass describes scale and organisation, not a traveller's motive; many visitors can still have different interests.
contrast.ru: «Массовый» описывает масштаб и организацию, а не мотив: интересы многочисленных посетителей могут различаться.

thanatourism.name: Dark tourism / thanatourism
thanatourism.rule: Visits to places associated with death, suffering or catastrophe. The category covers diverse sites and experiences; remembrance and learning are common but not universal motives.
examples: Auschwitz-Birkenau and the 9/11 Memorial require sensitive interpretation and respect for victims.

contrast.en: The terms overlap in school geography; some researchers use thanatourism more narrowly for travel motivated by encounters with death.
contrast.ru: В школьной географии термины пересекаются; некоторые исследователи сужают танатотуризм до поездок, мотивированных обращением к смерти.

ecotourism.name: Ecotourism
ecotourism.rule: Nature-based tourism that includes learning, limits environmental and cultural harm, and contributes to conservation and the well-being of host communities.
examples: A locally managed guided forest visit can support conservation if fees and visitor behaviour are managed appropriately.

contrast.en: A nature trip is not automatically ecotourism: examine management, conservation benefits and local participation.
contrast.ru: Поездка на природу не автоматически экотуризм: проверяй управление, пользу для охраны природы и участие жителей.

medical.name: Medical tourism
medical.rule: Travel outside a person's usual environment to use medical services such as diagnosis, treatment or rehabilitation. It may be domestic or international.
examples: Travelling to a specialist treatment centre is an example; destination alone does not establish price, quality or safety.

contrast.en: Medical tourism concerns medical care; wellness tourism primarily concerns maintaining well-being and need not involve treatment.
contrast.ru: Медицинский туризм связан с медицинской помощью; оздоровительный прежде всего поддерживает самочувствие и не обязательно включает лечение.

extreme.name: Adventure and extreme tourism
extreme.rule: Adventure tourism involves activities linked to landscapes, physical effort or perceived risk. Extreme tourism describes its more demanding or hazardous end, rather than a single official risk class.
examples: Classify a trip by its actual activity and conditions, not just by a remote destination name.

contrast.en: A guided lowland hike and a high-altitude ascent can both be adventure tourism but demand very different skills and safeguards.
contrast.ru: Прогулка с гидом и высотное восхождение могут быть приключенческим туризмом, но требуют совершенно разных навыков и мер защиты.

voluntourism.name: Voluntourism
voluntourism.rule: Travel that combines a visitor experience with voluntary work on a host project, often through a paid programme. Evaluate what the host community needs and what the visitor can competently contribute.
examples: A locally requested habitat survey with trained volunteers has a clearer purpose than an unspecified short visit to 'help'.

contrast.en: Good intentions or a fee do not prove benefit; participation must support local priorities rather than displace paid local work.
contrast.ru: Добрые намерения или взнос не доказывают пользу: участие должно отвечать местным приоритетам, а не вытеснять оплачиваемый труд жителей.

butler.title: Butler Model

stages.5: Stagnation — growth slows or levels off; environmental or service capacity may be strained
stages.6: Possible later paths — decline, stabilisation or rejuvenation; none is inevitable

butler.examples: The tourism-area life-cycle is a conceptual model of possible destination change. Stages can overlap, be interrupted or follow different paths. The curve is schematic: neither time nor visitor numbers are calibrated.

jamaica.title: Case study — Jamaica (mass tourism)
jamaica.facts: Jamaica is a Caribbean island destination. Use dated visitor, employment and economic data from the case-study source; distinguish overnight tourists from cruise visitors and direct from total economic contribution.
jamaica.attractions: Tropical climate; sandy beaches at Montego Bay; water sports along the coast; all-inclusive hotels in Negril; Negril nightlife; golf in Negril; caves at Ocho Rios.
jamaica.positives: Tourism can generate jobs, demand for local goods, tax receipts and infrastructure investment. The local share depends on ownership, purchasing and access to services.
jamaica.negatives: Possible costs include leakage through imports and overseas profit transfers, seasonal or insecure work, pressure on housing and water, and damage to coastal habitats. Assess evidence for particular places and businesses.
jamaica.management: All-inclusive resorts (controversial — money stays inside), community tourism initiatives, government regulation of new development.

antarctica.title: Case study — Antarctica (extreme tourism)
antarctica.facts: Antarctica has no permanent resident population; research stations host scientists and support staff, while tourists usually make seasonal visits. Remoteness, ice and rapidly changing weather complicate access and rescue.
antarctica.whyGrowing: Specialist transport and organised expeditions make visits possible. Demand for remote landscapes can increase pressure on sensitive sites; growth and visitor profiles must be checked against dated statistics.
antarctica.negatives: Tourism can disturb wildlife, introduce non-native organisms, generate emissions and create waste or spill risks. Disturbance may disrupt feeding and breeding; do not assume every touched egg is abandoned. Penguins are flightless, so oil harms insulation and swimming rather than flight.
antarctica.positives: Income for tour operators; awareness raised through tourism education.
antarctica.management: Tourism is subject to the Antarctic Treaty system, national authorisations and site guidance. Visitors must avoid disturbing wildlife, introducing non-native species and leaving waste; some protected areas require specific permission.

resourceReliance.intro: How societies depend on resources — energy, water, food. Sustainability concepts, Malthus vs Boserup, and key players.

resource.name: Resource
resource.rule: Something people can use to meet a need or achieve a purpose. Natural resources include water, soil, organisms, minerals and energy flows; usefulness depends on technology, access and demand.
examples: A forest is renewable only if regeneration can sustain harvesting; uranium is a finite mineral fuel.

contrast.en: Renewable stocks can be depleted if use exceeds regeneration; flow resources such as sunlight are not stored finite fuel deposits.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемые запасы истощаются, если использование превышает восстановление; поточные ресурсы, например солнечное излучение, не являются конечным топливным запасом.

carrying.name: Carrying capacity
carrying.rule: The population or level of activity that an environment can sustain over time under specified resource, technology and consumption conditions.
examples: A region may support different populations under different diets, farming methods and water supplies.

contrast.en: For human societies this is conditional and changeable, not a fixed worldwide headcount; trade can shift pressures elsewhere.

sustainability.title: Sustainability
sustainability.brundtland: Development that addresses present needs while preserving future generations' ability to meet theirs. It links environmental limits with human well-being and fairness between and within generations.
sustainability.sdgs: Seventeen linked global goals adopted in 2015 as part of the UN 2030 Agenda. They set objectives supported by targets and indicators for countries at all income levels.

brundtland.name: Sustainable development (Brundtland, 1987)
brundtland.rule: Development that addresses present needs while preserving future generations' ability to meet theirs. It links environmental limits with human well-being and fairness between and within generations.
examples: A water project should be affordable now and preserve reliable clean supplies and ecosystems for the future.

contrast.en: Sustainable development is broader than environmental protection or continuing GDP growth; examine social, economic and environmental outcomes together.
contrast.ru: Устойчивое развитие шире охраны природы или непрерывного роста ВВП; рассматривай социальные, экономические и экологические результаты вместе.

sdgs.rule: Seventeen linked global goals adopted in 2015 as part of the UN 2030 Agenda. They set objectives supported by targets and indicators for countries at all income levels.
examples: Goal 6 addresses water and sanitation; Goal 12 addresses consumption and production.

contrast.en: A goal is an intended outcome; adoption does not show that the outcome has been achieved.
contrast.ru: Цель — желаемый результат; её принятие не доказывает достижения.

energy.title: Energy sources
energy.renewable: Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biofuels
energy.nonRenewable: Non-renewable: coal, oil, natural gas and uranium fuel for nuclear power. Low-carbon is a separate classification.

solar.name: Solar energy
solar.rule: Energy from solar radiation. Photovoltaic cells convert light to electricity; solar thermal systems collect heat or use concentrated sunlight to generate power.
examples: A rooftop photovoltaic panel produces electricity in daylight, with lower output under many cloudy conditions.

contrast.en: Solar is renewable, but output varies with daylight and weather; installed capacity is not continuous generation.
contrast.ru: Солнечная энергия возобновляема, но выработка меняется с освещением и погодой; установленная мощность не равна постоянной выработке.

wind.name: Wind energy
wind.rule: Wind turbines transfer kinetic energy from moving air into mechanical rotation and then electricity. Wind is a replenished energy flow.
examples: A wind farm's annual generation depends on the wind resource as well as its installed capacity.

contrast.en: Wind speed and turbine operating limits determine output; turbines do not generate their rated power all the time.
contrast.ru: Выработка зависит от скорости ветра и рабочих ограничений турбины; номинальная мощность достигается не постоянно.

hydro.name: Hydropower
hydro.rule: Electricity generated by moving water driving turbines, often using a difference in water level. The water cycle replenishes river flows.
examples: A reservoir can store water for later generation, but its storage and inflow are finite.

contrast.en: Renewable does not mean impact-free: dams alter sediment, habitats and land use; drought can reduce generation.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемое не означает безвредное: плотины меняют наносы, местообитания и землепользование; засуха может снизить выработку.

geothermal.rule: Useful heat from within Earth, accessed for heating or, at suitable temperatures, electricity generation.
examples: Hot underground fluids can supply a district-heating network.

contrast.en: A renewable classification does not guarantee every local reservoir is inexhaustible; extraction and recharge must be managed.
contrast.ru: Отнесение к возобновляемым источникам не делает каждый местный резервуар неисчерпаемым: нужны управление отбором и восполнением.

biofuels.name: Biofuels and biomass
biofuels.rule: Biomass is recently living organic material used as an energy source. Biofuels are fuels made from it, including ethanol, biodiesel and biogas.
examples: Using crop residues differs from clearing forest to grow an energy crop.

contrast.en: Renewability requires replacement of the biomass; carbon emissions depend on cultivation, land-use change, processing and combustion.
contrast.ru: Возобновляемость требует восстановления биомассы; выбросы зависят от выращивания, изменения землепользования, переработки и сжигания.

fossilFuels.name: Fossil fuels
fossilFuels.rule: Coal, oil and natural gas formed from ancient organic material over geological time. Burning them releases stored chemical energy and carbon dioxide.
examples: Gas can produce electricity on demand, but combustion still releases CO₂.

contrast.en: They are non-renewable on human timescales; a deposit being large does not make it renewable.
contrast.ru: В масштабе человеческой жизни они невозобновляемы; большой запас не делает ресурс возобновляемым.

nuclear.name: Nuclear fission energy
nuclear.rule: Power stations release energy by splitting heavy atomic nuclei, usually using uranium fuel; the heat is used to generate electricity.
examples: Compare fuel supply, construction, operation and waste management when judging an energy option.

contrast.en: Nuclear power is low-carbon over its life cycle but uses finite mineral fuel and creates waste requiring long-term management; low-carbon and renewable are different categories.
contrast.ru: Атомная энергетика имеет низкие выбросы углерода за жизненный цикл, но использует конечное топливо и создаёт отходы для длительного обращения; низкоуглеродное и возобновляемое — разные признаки.

malthusBoserup.title: Malthus vs Boserup
malthusBoserup.malthus: Malthus argued that unchecked population could grow faster than food supply, creating pressure restrained by checks such as reduced births or higher mortality. This is a historical argument with assumptions, not a universal forecast.
malthusBoserup.boserup: Boserup argued that population pressure can encourage more intensive land use, including shorter fallow periods, more labour and changes in farming techniques, raising output per unit of land.

malthus.name: Malthusian population model
malthus.rule: Malthus argued that unchecked population could grow faster than food supply, creating pressure restrained by checks such as reduced births or higher mortality. This is a historical argument with assumptions, not a universal forecast.
examples: Compare the model's assumed growth paths with evidence on yields, fertility and access to food.

contrast.en: A model of population pressure does not explain every famine: access, inequality, conflict and technology also matter.
contrast.ru: Модель демографического давления не объясняет любой голод: важны доступ, неравенство, конфликты и технологии.

boserup.name: Boserup's agricultural intensification model
boserup.rule: Boserup argued that population pressure can encourage more intensive land use, including shorter fallow periods, more labour and changes in farming techniques, raising output per unit of land.
examples: More frequent cultivation can feed more people while increasing labour needs and pressure on soils.

contrast.en: Higher output per hectare need not mean higher output per hour of labour. Innovation is possible, not guaranteed or free of environmental costs.
contrast.ru: Больший выпуск с гектара не обязательно означает больший выпуск за час труда. Новшества возможны, но не гарантированы и могут иметь экологическую цену.

waterStress.title: Water stress
waterStress.description: Pressure from water use relative to available water. SDG indicator 6.4.2 compares freshwater withdrawals with renewable freshwater resources after allowing for environmental water needs, expressed as a percentage.

definition.name: Water stress
definition.rule: Pressure from water use relative to available water. SDG indicator 6.4.2 compares freshwater withdrawals with renewable freshwater resources after allowing for environmental water needs, expressed as a percentage.
examples: A national annual average can hide severe seasonal or basin-level shortages.

contrast.en: Water stress is a pressure indicator; water security is broader and includes reliable access, water quality, ecosystems and protection from water-related harm. Different indices use different thresholds.
contrast.ru: Водный стресс — показатель нагрузки; водная безопасность шире и включает надёжный доступ, качество воды, экосистемы и защиту от связанного с водой ущерба. Пороговые значения разных индексов различаются.

causes.name: Drivers of water stress
causes.rule: Stress can rise when withdrawals increase, renewable supply falls, or water needed by ecosystems is left out of allocation. Irrigation, industry, households and drought all affect the balance.
examples: Expanding irrigation without a water budget can raise withdrawals beyond sustainable availability.

contrast.en: Scarce rainfall is only one cause; high demand can stress a relatively wet basin, while poor water quality can restrict usable supply.
contrast.ru: Малые осадки — лишь одна причина: высокий спрос нагружает и относительно влажный бассейн, а загрязнение ограничивает пригодную воду.

solutions.name: Managing water stress
solutions.rule: Combine demand management, leakage reduction, appropriate reuse, protection of water quality and ecosystems, and reliable supply planning at basin scale.
examples: Judge an option by water saved, energy use, affordability and effects downstream.

contrast.en: More efficient irrigation does not automatically save water across a basin if saved water expands irrigated area or reduces return flows.
contrast.ru: Эффективное орошение не автоматически экономит воду бассейна, если высвобождённый объём расширяет полив или уменьшает возвратный сток.

foodSecurity.title: Food security
foodSecurity.factors: Availability, access, utilisation and stability: population, water, climate, soils, incomes, conflict and trade affect these in different ways.

definition.name: Food security
definition.rule: People have food security when they can consistently obtain enough safe, nutritious food for a healthy active life. Four connected dimensions are availability, access, utilisation and stability over time.
examples: A functioning food market addresses availability; sufficient household income addresses access.

contrast.en: A country can produce enough food while some households cannot afford it. Food insecurity is broader than famine and is not the same as low national self-sufficiency.
contrast.ru: Страна может производить достаточно пищи, но часть семей не может её купить. Продовольственная незащищённость шире массового голода и не равна низкому самообеспечению страны.

drivers.name: Drivers of food insecurity
drivers.rule: Crop losses can reduce availability; conflict, displacement or low income can block access; unsafe water or poor diet can impair utilisation. Repeated shocks undermine stability.
examples: A price rise may make food inaccessible to low-income households without a complete production failure.

contrast.en: Food insecurity can occur where shops contain food. Identify which dimension fails rather than assuming too little food is grown.
contrast.ru: Нехватка продовольственной безопасности возможна при полных магазинах. Укажи нарушенную сторону вместо предположения, что всегда мало выращено.

solutions.name: Improving food security
solutions.rule: Match action to the failing dimension: resilient farming and storage support supply; income or food assistance supports access; safe water and appropriate nutrition support utilisation; planning helps stability.

contrast.en: Increasing yield alone cannot solve insecurity caused by lost income, exclusion or conflict.
contrast.ru: Одно повышение урожайности не устраняет проблемы из-за утраты дохода, исключения из доступа или конфликта.

un.name: United Nations and international agencies
un.rule: Intergovernmental organisations support cooperation through shared goals, evidence, technical assistance and programmes. Different UN bodies have different mandates and powers.
examples: FAO supports food and agriculture information; SDG progress relies on action by many partners.

contrast.en: An agreed global goal differs from national implementation; avoid treating all UN bodies as a single government or claiming none has any legal authority.

ngos.name: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs)
ngos.rule: Organisations outside government that work on public or community purposes, for example through advocacy, research or services. Funding and accountability arrangements vary.
examples: Assess a project by local participation, evidence of outcomes and transparent use of funds.

contrast.en: Non-governmental does not mean funded only by donations, or automatically representative of every local voice.

businesses.rule: Businesses produce goods and services; TNCs organise or control activities in more than one country. Their supply chains, investment and purchasing decisions affect resource use and jobs.

contrast.en: A company pledge is a stated intention; verified outcomes require a baseline, scope, dates and measured results.

governments.name: National and local governments
governments.rule: Governments can set rules, taxes, budgets and infrastructure priorities and provide public services. Their capacity, responsibilities and effectiveness differ across places.
examples: A water policy needs monitoring, service investment and clear responsibilities as well as targets.

contrast.en: Announcing a policy differs from funding, enforcing and evaluating it.
contrast.ru: Объявление политики отличается от её финансирования, исполнения и оценки.

citizens.name: Citizens and consumers
citizens.rule: People influence resource decisions through purchasing, everyday practices, civic participation and collective action. Available choices depend on income, services and institutions.
examples: A household can reduce waste, while collection systems and product design affect what reduction is feasible.

contrast.en: Individual consumption choices and structural policy act at different scales and can reinforce each other.
contrast.ru: Личное потребление и системная политика действуют на разных уровнях и могут дополнять друг друга.

climateZones.items: Polar, Temperate, Arid, Tropical, Mediterranean, Mountainous

polar.name: Polar climate
polar.rule: A climate with very cool summers; in the Köppen classification, the warmest month's mean temperature is below 10°C. Tundra climates can rise above freezing in summer; ice-cap climates do not reach a monthly mean above 0°C.
examples: Compare tundra coasts with the interior Antarctic ice sheet; their summer conditions differ.

contrast.en: The polar circles are astronomical latitude lines, not exact climate boundaries. Polar does not mean every day is below freezing.
contrast.ru: Полярные круги — астрономические линии широты, а не точные климатические границы. Полярный климат не означает мороз каждый день.

temperate.name: Temperate climates
temperate.rule: A broad school-geography grouping of climates between tropical and polar extremes, with seasonal temperature differences. Maritime influence, continentality and circulation produce different rainfall and temperature regimes.
examples: An oceanic west coast usually has a smaller annual temperature range than a continental interior at similar latitude.

contrast.en: Temperate is not a guarantee of mild winters or rain in every season; classify the specific climate rather than using latitude alone.
contrast.ru: Умеренный не гарантирует мягкую зиму или дождь в любой сезон; определяй конкретный тип, а не только широту.

arid.name: Arid climate
arid.rule: A climate with a persistent moisture deficit: precipitation is small relative to potential evaporation and transpiration. Many deserts have under about 250 mm annually, but classification also depends on temperature and rainfall seasonality.
examples: A cool desert can receive little rain without having hot-desert summer temperatures.

contrast.en: Arid describes water balance, not heat; deserts can be hot or cold. One rainfall threshold is a school shortcut.
contrast.ru: Аридность описывает водный баланс, а не жару; пустыни бывают жаркими и холодными. Единый порог осадков — школьное упрощение.

tropical.name: Tropical climates
tropical.rule: In the Köppen system, tropical climates have mean temperatures of at least 18°C in every month. Rainfall distinguishes rainforest, monsoon and savanna types.
examples: A tropical rainforest is wet through the year; a tropical savanna has a marked dry season.

contrast.en: The geographic tropics also contain dry deserts and cool high mountains. English tropical climate is not identical to the narrower Russian climatic belt label «тропический пояс».
contrast.ru: Между тропиками есть также сухие пустыни и холодные высокогорья. Английское tropical climate не полностью совпадает с русским названием пояса «тропический».

mediterranean.name: Mediterranean climate
mediterranean.rule: A climate characterised by dry summers and relatively wetter, mild winters, found around the Mediterranean and in some other west-coast regions. Summers may be hot or warm depending on subtype.
examples: Central Chile and parts of California share a dry-summer rainfall pattern with the Mediterranean basin.

contrast.en: Mediterranean is a climate type, not only a location. Fire risk also depends on vegetation, ignition and land management.
contrast.ru: Средиземноморский — тип климата, а не только местоположение. Пожарный риск зависит также от растительности, источника огня и управления землёй.

mountainous.name: Mountain / highland climates
mountainous.rule: Local climates shaped strongly by elevation, slope aspect and relief. Air temperature generally decreases with altitude in the troposphere, while windward and leeward slopes can receive very different precipitation.
examples: Two sites at the same latitude can have different climates if one is high in the mountains.

contrast.en: About 6.5°C per kilometre is a standard average environmental lapse rate, not a constant at every mountain or time; inversions can reverse the gradient.
contrast.ru: Около 6,5°C на километр — стандартное среднее убывание температуры, а не постоянная для каждой горы и момента; при инверсии знак может измениться.

latitudeSun.description: When sunlight strikes a surface at a lower angle, the same incoming beam is spread over a larger area. Averaged over the year, high latitudes receive less solar energy per unit area than low latitudes.

physics.name: Solar angle and latitude
physics.rule: When sunlight strikes a surface at a lower angle, the same incoming beam is spread over a larger area. Averaged over the year, high latitudes receive less solar energy per unit area than low latitudes.

contrast.en: Solar angle varies with latitude, season and time of day; the Sun is not vertically overhead at the equator every day.

tilt.name: Axial tilt and seasons
tilt.rule: Earth's rotation axis is tilted about 23.5° from the perpendicular to its orbital plane. As Earth orbits, this changes day length and solar height in each hemisphere, producing opposite seasons.
examples: In June the Northern Hemisphere has longer days and higher midday Sun than in December.

review.russianTerm: Наклон земной оси и времена года

contrast.en: The angle to the orbital plane itself is about 66.5°. Seasons primarily arise from tilt, not changing Earth–Sun distance.
contrast.ru: К самой плоскости орбиты угол около 66,5°. Сезоны определяются прежде всего наклоном, а не изменением расстояния до Солнца.

circulation.title: Atmospheric circulation cells
circulation.items: Idealised mean cells: Hadley roughly 0–30°, Ferrel roughly 30–60°, Polar roughly 60–90°, in each hemisphere. Their boundaries shift.

hadley.name: Hadley cell
hadley.rule: A tropical overturning circulation: air rises near the shifting tropical rain belt, moves poleward aloft and generally sinks in the subtropics. Surface trade winds return air toward the convergence zone.
examples: Subtropical descending air helps explain many dry belts, alongside ocean currents and relief.

contrast.en: The three-cell diagram is a long-term, zonally averaged model; ascent is not fixed exactly at 0° and descent is not fixed at 30°.
contrast.ru: Трёхъячеечная схема — многолетняя модель, усреднённая по долготе; подъём не закреплён строго на 0°, а опускание на 30°.

ferrel.name: Ferrel cell
ferrel.rule: The idealised mid-latitude mean circulation, with surface air generally moving poleward and an equatorward return aloft. It is thermally indirect and maintained largely through mid-latitude weather systems and their heat and momentum transfers.
examples: Prevailing westerlies are a mean tendency, not the wind direction at every time and place.

contrast.en: It is not a simple closed convection loop mechanically pushed by adjacent cells; actual mid-latitude winds are highly variable.
contrast.ru: Это не простая замкнутая конвективная петля, которую механически толкают соседние ячейки; реальные ветры сильно меняются.

polar.name: Polar cell
polar.rule: In the idealised circulation model, cold air sinks at high latitudes and flows equatorward near the surface, with ascent toward subpolar latitudes and return flow aloft.
examples: Near-surface polar easterlies result from the mean pressure pattern and Earth's rotation.

contrast.en: The polar front shifts and is irregular; the polar cell is not the same feature as the stratospheric polar vortex.
contrast.ru: Полярный фронт смещается и неоднороден; полярная ячейка и стратосферный полярный вихрь — разные явления.

pressure.title: High & low pressure
pressure.high: A region with surface pressure higher than its surroundings. Descending air often warms by compression, lowering relative humidity and suppressing cloud formation.
pressure.low: A region with surface pressure lower than its surroundings. Converging air and ascent often promote cooling, condensation and unsettled weather when enough moisture is present.

high.name: High-pressure system (anticyclone)
high.rule: A region with surface pressure higher than its surroundings. Descending air often warms by compression, lowering relative humidity and suppressing cloud formation.
examples: A clear anticyclonic winter night can cool strongly by radiation.

contrast.en: High pressure need not mean high temperature or clear skies: winter fog and low cloud can persist. Wind strength depends on pressure gradient, not the label high or low.
contrast.ru: Высокое давление не обязательно означает высокую температуру или ясное небо: зимой возможны туман и низкая облачность. Сила ветра зависит от градиента давления, а не названия системы.

low.name: Low-pressure system (cyclone / depression)
low.rule: A region with surface pressure lower than its surroundings. Converging air and ascent often promote cooling, condensation and unsettled weather when enough moisture is present.
examples: Closely spaced isobars indicate a strong pressure gradient and usually stronger winds.

contrast.en: A low is not defined by a universal 980 hPa threshold. Mid-latitude depressions often have fronts; tropical cyclones have a different warm-core structure.
contrast.ru: Циклон не определяется универсальным порогом 980 гПа. Умеренные циклоны часто имеют фронты; тропические отличаются тёплым ядром.

tropicalStorms.title: Tropical storms
tropicalStorms.description: A tropical cyclone is an organised rotating low-pressure system with a warm core over tropical or subtropical waters. Formation is favoured by deep warm water, moist unstable air, a disturbance, weak vertical wind shear and sufficient Coriolis effect.

formation.name: Tropical cyclone formation
formation.rule: A tropical cyclone is an organised rotating low-pressure system with a warm core over tropical or subtropical waters. Formation is favoured by deep warm water, moist unstable air, a disturbance, weak vertical wind shear and sufficient Coriolis effect.
examples: Condensation releases latent heat; the circulation draws further warm moist air from the ocean.

contrast.en: About 27°C and more than roughly 5° from the equator are useful typical conditions, not absolute guarantees or exception-free boundaries.
contrast.ru: Около 27°C и удаление более примерно 5° от экватора — типичные ориентиры, а не достаточные условия или границы без исключений.

naming.name: Hurricane, typhoon and tropical cyclone
naming.rule: Hurricane and typhoon are regional names for sufficiently strong tropical cyclones: hurricane in the Atlantic and northeast/central Pacific, typhoon in the northwest Pacific. Other basins use their own cyclone classifications.
examples: Storm surge and heavy rainfall can be dangerous even when the wind category is relatively low.

contrast.en: The Saffir–Simpson scale rates sustained hurricane wind, not rainfall or storm surge; it is not the official classification used identically in every basin.
contrast.ru: Шкала Саффира–Симпсона оценивает устойчивый ветер урагана, а не осадки или нагон; во всех бассейнах она не применяется одинаково.

impacts.name: Tropical cyclone hazards and impacts
impacts.rule: Wind, heavy rain and storm surge can damage structures, inundate land and trigger landslides. Losses depend on exposure, vulnerability, warning and capacity to respond as well as storm characteristics.
examples: Flooding can directly damage homes; interruption of clean-water supply can create further health risks.

review.russianTerm: Опасные процессы и последствия тропического циклона

contrast.en: Storm surge is an abnormal rise above the predicted tide, not simply one large breaking wave. State the initiating event when separating primary from secondary effects.
contrast.ru: Штормовой нагон — аномальное повышение уровня относительно ожидаемого прилива, а не просто одна большая волна. При делении на первичные и вторичные последствия укажи исходное событие.

enso.title: El Niño / La Niña / Normal
enso.normal: In the usual equatorial Pacific pattern, easterly trade winds push warm surface water westward and help maintain cooler upwelled water in the east. ENSO-neutral means neither El Niño nor La Niña conditions dominate.
enso.elNino: The warm phase of ENSO: unusually warm surface water in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific is coupled with atmospheric changes, commonly weaker trade winds and reduced eastern upwelling.
enso.laNina: The cool phase of ENSO: unusually cool surface water in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific is coupled with atmospheric changes, often stronger trade winds and enhanced upwelling.

normal.name: ENSO-neutral Pacific conditions
normal.rule: In the usual equatorial Pacific pattern, easterly trade winds push warm surface water westward and help maintain cooler upwelled water in the east. ENSO-neutral means neither El Niño nor La Niña conditions dominate.
examples: The western warm pool favours convection, while nutrient-rich upwelling supports eastern Pacific ecosystems.

review.russianTerm: Нейтральные условия ENSO в Тихом океане

contrast.en: Neutral does not mean no weather extremes or no variability; ENSO is only one influence on climate.
contrast.ru: Нейтральная фаза не означает отсутствие экстремальной погоды или изменчивости; ENSO — лишь один из факторов климата.

elNino.name: El Niño
elNino.rule: The warm phase of ENSO: unusually warm surface water in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific is coupled with atmospheric changes, commonly weaker trade winds and reduced eastern upwelling.
examples: Reduced upwelling can reduce nutrient supply; effects vary with event strength, season and location.

contrast.en: El Niño changes probabilities of regional weather, not a fixed list of guaranteed floods or droughts. Events recur irregularly, commonly within a 2–7-year range.
contrast.ru: Эль-Ниньо меняет вероятности региональной погоды, а не гарантирует заданный список наводнений и засух. События повторяются нерегулярно, часто в интервале 2–7 лет.

laNina.name: La Niña
laNina.rule: The cool phase of ENSO: unusually cool surface water in the central/eastern equatorial Pacific is coupled with atmospheric changes, often stronger trade winds and enhanced upwelling.
examples: The phase can favour wetter conditions in some regions and drier conditions in others, depending on season.

contrast.en: Regional impacts are not exact mirror images of every El Niño event; an ENSO phase alone is not a local forecast.
contrast.ru: Региональные последствия не являются точным зеркальным отражением каждого Эль-Ниньо; фаза ENSO сама по себе не местный прогноз.

haiyan.title: Case study — Typhoon Haiyan (Nov 2013)
haiyan.scale: A very powerful tropical cyclone with destructive winds and coastal storm-surge flooding. Surge depth varied by location; a single value does not describe the whole coast.

seep.social: Social: GIZ’s May 2014 assessment records more than 6,000 deaths and about 4 million displaced people using earlier situation reports. Displaced is not the same measure as homeless.
seep.economic: Economic: homes, businesses and transport infrastructure were damaged; losses depend on which assets and reporting period are counted.
seep.environmental: Environmental: storm surge flooded coastal land, while strong winds damaged vegetation and spread debris.
seep.political: Governance: the assessment identified gaps between hazard forecasts, public understanding and evacuation decisions.

responses.local: Local: residents and responders carried out evacuation and rescue under severe disruption.
responses.government: Government: storm warnings and evacuation orders were issued, but some evacuation centres were themselves exposed to storm surge.
responses.shortTerm: Short term: emergency relief addressed shelter, food, safe water and medical needs.
responses.longTerm: Long term: the GIZ assessment recommended clearer warnings, better hazard maps and safer evacuation centres; recommendations are not evidence of completed rebuilding.

bigDry.title: Case study — Australia’s Millennium Drought
bigDry.summary: A prolonged drought affected southern Australia. Dates depend on region and indicator: the South Australian government describes the River Murray episode as late 2001–2010. Low rainfall and over-allocation combined to reduce flows and threaten water supplies.

seep.social: Social: Adelaide’s supply and Lower Lakes communities were threatened; restrictions and new drinking-water pipelines were used.
seep.economic: Economic: irrigation allocations were restricted, placing pressure on agriculture and horticulture. Avoid applying one annual loss estimate to every drought year.
seep.environmental: Environmental: low lake levels exposed acid sulfate soils; salinity increased and wetlands lost connectivity.
seep.political: Governance: drought experience contributed to basin-wide planning, environmental water recovery and changes in water management.
